changes: Hello from the maintainer. The project is alive and this firmware is still being worked on — it has not been abandoned. I had to leave other platforms where I posted project updates for certain reasons, so GitHub is now the only place where information about this firmware is published. Please report problems and send suggestions through the Issues page at https://github.com/sowarden/hh71vm-openwrt/issues, and there is now a Discussions section at https://github.com/sowarden/hh71vm-openwrt/discussions for questions, ideas and anything else about OpenWrt on the HH71 and HH71VM. Thank you to everyone who tests these builds and reports what breaks — that is what makes each release better. The changes in this build are listed below.

Security: fix a serious flaw where text that came from outside the router was treated as page markup. The body or sender of an SMS, an operator name broadcast by the mobile network, an AT answer and the name inside an imported Xray share link were all affected. A message written to exploit it could run commands with your router's administrator rights the moment you opened the page that showed it. Every such value is now shown as text.

Security: LAN and Wi-Fi clients can no longer reach the Qualcomm modem half at 192.168.225.1. It answers a root telnet with no password, an unauthenticated control service, and a guest-writable file share that this router runs programs from, so until now any device on your network, including anyone who knew the default Wi-Fi key, could take over both halves of the device. The router's own access to the modem is unchanged, so nothing in OpenWrt loses a feature.

The new firewall rule is called Block-LAN-to-Qualcomm and appears under Network > Firewall > Traffic Rules. Disable it there, rather than deleting it, if you need to reach the stock modem web interface or its telnet directly from a computer; a deleted rule is put back after the next sysupgrade.

New: carrier SIM lock control on Modem > Overview. It says whether a carrier lock is in force, whether the SIM in the router is refused by it, and how many unlock attempts are left, and it can remove the lock either with an unlock code or without one. It lives in the base image so that a router refusing its own SIM can still be recovered without installing anything first.
New: the Overview page and the status dashboard say so when the modem is refusing the SIM because of a carrier lock, instead of only reporting that the SIM is not ready.
New: Extra Tools can lock this router to the network of the SIM currently in it. Removing that lock is done from Modem > Overview.

Removing a carrier lock without an unlock code is now offered on every modem. It used to be refused unless the Qualcomm firmware was the exact build it had been tested on, which meant nobody with a different build could try it or report back. The page now warns when your build is untested or cannot be read, and asks you to report the result with your firmware version. Trying is safe either way: no unlock code is sent and none of the ten attempts is used.

New: SMS to Telegram messages are built from a template you can edit. Placeholders are replaced by the sender, this router's own SIM number, the message text, the time the message was sent, the router's own clock, the number of parts, a note about missing parts, the SIM store and the router hostname.

New: SMS to Telegram can send messages with Telegram formatting. Choose HTML, MarkdownV2 or plain text. Your template's own markup is sent as written, while the values put into it are escaped, so a message that contains < or * cannot break the formatting or forge any of it.

If Telegram rejects a template's formatting, the message is now still delivered once as plain text and the SMS to Telegram page says that it happened. A mistake in a template no longer stops messages arriving.

SMS to Telegram: a failed connection is no longer reported as an HTTP error blaming the bot token. The message now asks you to check internet access and the router clock, because this router has no battery-backed clock and a wrong date makes the secure connection to Telegram fail.

Fix the firmware updater appearing to lose the connection during an upgrade. The download and install now run as a background job that the page follows, instead of inside a single request that the web interface gave up on after twenty seconds and that was then killed after sixty, leaving a partial image in RAM and never reporting the failure.

The check for firmware updates is now roughly twice as fast and no longer reports at random that older release information could not be verified. It used to download more than a megabyte it did not need and spend about half of its time budget re-reading that same data, leaving too little time to collect the release history; it now reads a small feed instead, so the check finishes sooner and the list of previous releases is complete.

Fix SMS to Telegram forwarding half of a long message. A message whose parts are still arriving is now held until it is complete, or for ten minutes, after which it is forwarded with a note naming the missing parts. Previously the first part was sent on its own, the whole message was sent again as a duplicate once the rest arrived, and with SIM deletion enabled the late parts went out as an orphaned fragment.

Fix SMS to Telegram writing to flash every fifteen seconds while the modem or Telegram was unreachable, which was about 5,700 writes a day. Its state is now written only when something in it actually changes, records for messages that have left the modem are eventually dropped instead of accumulating for ever, and message fingerprints are no longer recomputed on every poll.

Fix the modem daemon restarting on every WAN event, which dropped whatever was in flight, including an SMS submission that can legitimately take minutes. A working modem channel is now left alone, and a channel that is down is retried immediately instead of waiting out its backoff.

Fix the first long SMS sent after each modem daemon start always using the same concatenation reference, which could make a recipient's phone merge two different messages into one. The generator is now seeded from the system random source.
The saved APN file is now created readable only by root. It can contain the APN password.
Fix Xray following the first interface change of a burst instead of the last, so its rules no longer end up matching an interface state that has already been replaced.

Xray no longer accepts an arbitrary clock from its connectivity probe. A probe answer can no longer move this router's clock by years, which would have broken certificate validation for package installs, firmware updates and Telegram.
Xray's status page no longer reports a reconnect when Xray is not actually running.

sysupgrade now refuses a compressed firmware image instead of writing it. Nothing this project publishes is compressed, and splitting a compressed image could have shifted the boundary between the kernel and the root filesystem.
Fix the external storage service looking for its startup scripts under the default path when a different share target was configured.

Theme: the navigation drawer on a phone now behaves like a proper dialog. While it is closed its links can no longer be reached by keyboard or read by a screen reader, opening it moves the focus into it and closing it puts the focus back on the menu button, and every page starts with a link that jumps straight to the content.

Theme: fix dropdown lists being cut off at the edge of a card or table on phones and tablets. This affected the firewall zone choosers, the interface zone selectors, the Save and Apply menu inside a card and the modem dialogs.

Theme: error notifications are no longer dismissed automatically after ten seconds, so a failed firmware upgrade or a failed SMS is not missed. The tray also announces new messages to screen readers, and dismissing a notification no longer presses a button that belonged to the notification itself.
Theme: raise text and control contrast in the light theme to meet WCAG AA, and make the keyboard focus indicator visible in Windows high contrast mode, where it previously disappeared completely.
Theme: the status dashboard no longer rearranges itself while you read it. Cards keep their place instead of jumping between columns every time one of them changes height.

Theme: phone improvements. The unread SMS indicator stays visible in the top bar instead of hiding inside a closed drawer, copy buttons are visible and large enough to press on a touch screen, small controls meet the minimum touch size, and dialogs no longer hide their buttons behind the browser toolbar.
Theme: the words the theme adds itself are now translatable along with the rest of the interface.
Theme: a firmware update that changes only a page's JavaScript now reaches the browser instead of being served from its cache.

Theme: jumping to a heading or to an invalid form field no longer lands underneath the fixed top bar, a stale status strip explains why its values are dimmed, and raw daemon messages in the top bar are replaced by a short explanation with the detail kept in a tooltip.
Theme: on a touch screen an open dropdown list no longer stretches across the full width of the screen; it stays the width of the control it belongs to.
Theme: fix the text of a long button touching its own border on a narrow phone screen. Labels such as "Reconnect control channel" now wrap onto a second line instead of overflowing.
Copy confirmations now appear in the notification area at the top of the page, like every other message in the interface, instead of as a separate bar at the bottom of the screen.
Fix the Copy button on the Messages page never finishing. The text did reach the clipboard, but the button kept spinning and no confirmation ever appeared.
Release notes are no longer limited to twelve short lines, so a release can describe everything it changed.
